solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Trudge through mud? Page in cloth’s damaged

indicators.note: one item placed inside another is housed within it
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for page
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A damaged tablecloth with a page stuck in it, after someone has tramped through mud.
explanation.walkthrough: The page goes into the cloth letters and the whole lot is then mixed. Chambers gives splotch as a variant of splodge, which as a verb means to trudge heavily through mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Splodge, and its variant, is a dictionary verb for plodding heavily through wet, muddy ground; the question mark flags the rarer sense.

clue.text: Scottish reel like this requires doctor being called up

indicators.note: in a down entry, being called up means being read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: so means in this way
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A Scottish dance seems to need a doctor summoned to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Soom is Scots for swim, and swim can mean to reel or feel giddy, as when one's head swims.
explanation.definitionFit: Soom is the Scots form of swim, and a swimming head is one that reels with dizziness.

clue.text: Firework or taper set off before start of dinner

indicators.note: setting something off disturbs it, so the letters are moved about
the start of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: taken as written for mixing
the opening letter of dinner

explanation.surface: A firework or a lit taper goes off just as dinner begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A petard was a small explosive charge, and Chambers also lists it as a kind of firework or cracker.

clue.text: A cracker taking look on weighing scales

blocks.note: la is an old exclamation meaning look! or behold
a tron was a public weighing machine, chiefly in Scotland

explanation.surface: A cracker, perhaps of the Christmas kind, being weighed on kitchen scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places one part after the other in this down entry. 'Cracker' here is a safecracker, a robber.
explanation.definitionFit: A latron is an obsolete word for a robber or bandit, and a cracker is a thief who breaks into safes.

clue.text: A stunner, damn fantastic, out of this world

indicators.note: something fantastic is wildly imagined, so these letters are freely reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gushing over a gorgeous person: a damn fantastic stunner, simply out of this world.
explanation.definitionFit: Transmundane means beyond the physical world, literally the sense of the idiom about something heavenly.

clue.text: What’s used in polish, unadulterated but with elements switched

indicators.note: the two parts of the word trade places, front portion moving to the back

blocks.note: sincere originally meant pure, unmixed

explanation.surface: A description of polish: pure stuff, but with its chemical elements swapped about.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN and CERE change places to give CERESIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceresin is a white mineral wax refined from ozokerite and used in polishes and candles.

clue.text: Like a leaf cluster, full-toned in a petal, i.e. splayed

indicators.note: something splayed is spread out of its order, so the letters are rearranged
one item is placed inside the mixed letters

blocks.note: a rich sound is full in tone
taken as written for mixing

explanation.surface: A botanist describes a flower whose petal is opened out, rich in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Perichaetial describes the perichaetium, the cluster of leaves surrounding the reproductive organs of a moss.

clue.text: After dinner, last of meal consumed ran

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone
something consumed is taken inside, so it sits within another part

blocks.note: once you have had dinner you are fed
final letter of meal

explanation.surface: After dinner the last of the meal was eaten and the diners left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After dinner' looks like a time phrase but describes a state: fed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fled is a past tense of flee, which is to run away from danger.

clue.text: Façade, fine blend of three?

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
refers to the answer to 3-down, written out in words

explanation.surface: A building's façade seems to be a fine mixture of three styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three' is a cross-reference to 3-down, LATRON, spelt out unusually in words; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A frontal is the decorated front of a building, its façade, as well as an altar hanging.

clue.text: Instrument, not loud, in protective covering

indicators.note: not means the following item is left out of the word

blocks.note: a woodwind instrument
f is forte, loud in music

explanation.surface: A quiet instrument kept in its protective case.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious instrument is the answer itself, but it is the definition that sits at the end: lute is also a clay or cement seal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lute is a clay or cement paste used as a sealing coat to protect joints and surfaces.

clue.text: Like Carthage, according to old orator, consequence coming in endless deferral

definitions.text: Like Carthage, according to old orator

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it
without its end, the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: an end is a result or outcome
a delay defers something

explanation.surface: A history note on Carthage and a consequence of endless postponement.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder ended speeches with 'Carthago delenda est', Carthage must be destroyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Delenda is Latin for things to be destroyed, as Cato insisted Carthage must be in his famous refrain.

clue.text: Bore, weak without money as introduction

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the item is taken away

blocks.note: meagre means thin or feeble
M is the abbreviation for money, removed here from the front

explanation.surface: A dull person, weak and penniless, being introduced at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is not a tedious person but a tidal wave in a river; 'as introduction' says the removed M is the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, the surge wave running up an estuary such as the Severn or Trent.

clue.text: Pet has almost run in for a scratch?

definitions.note: the question mark: what one wears in place of a scratch wig

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes
one item sits inside the other

blocks.note: a Pekinese dog is a common pet
run cut short

explanation.surface: A pet dog has almost dashed inside to scratch itself.
explanation.walkthrough: A scratch is a scratch wig, a short wig covering only part of the head; the scratch is not something a dog does.
explanation.definitionFit: A peruke is a wig, the kind of hairpiece that might replace a scratch wig.

clue.text: Ancient statue, with animals – it creates a buzz

blocks.note: in ancient Egypt the ka was the soul, also a statue of the dead person housing it
a zoo is a collection of animals

explanation.surface: An old statue surrounded by animals is causing a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A kazoo is a toy instrument that makes a buzzing sound when you hum into it.

clue.text: Man leaving comfortable seat – it’s fragrant

indicators.note: one part leaving means it is taken away from the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
an ottoman is a padded seat or couch

explanation.surface: A man gets up from a cosy armchair and finds it smells nice.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a variant of attar, a fragrant essential oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Little bell, round, found in Sri Lanka

indicators.note: something found in another is sitting inside it

blocks.note: CL is Sri Lanka's international vehicle registration code
a rota is a round or cycle of duties

explanation.surface: A little round bell turned up in Sri Lanka.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like the bell's shape, but it is the duty rota.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotal is a small spherical bell with a loose pellet inside, like a sleigh bell.

clue.text: Seaman causing damage round old bark

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
an obsolete word for rind, the bark of a tree

explanation.surface: A sailor who damages an old sailing ship, a barque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' tempts as a ship, but it is tree bark, in an old spelling found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a sailor, a seaman who works aboard ship.

clue.text: Typical element irritated by misspelt notices

indicators.note: a misspelt word has its letters in the wrong order

blocks.note: cross means annoyed
taken as written for mixing

explanation.surface: An office worker annoyed by badly spelt notices.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-section is a representative sample, a part that typifies the whole group.

clue.text: Gouge page enveloped by one working throughout innings?

indicators.note: being enveloped means wrapped inside another

blocks.note: the cricket scorer is busy for the whole innings
standard abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer gouges a page in his book during a long innings.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a team's turn at batting in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorper is an engraver's gouge, a chisel-like tool for hollowing out metal or wood.

clue.text: Boater maybe going round a fen, rippling – it can be full during ebb-tide

definitions.text: it can be full during ebb-tide

indicators.note: going round means encircling the other part
rippling water is disturbed, so the letters are shaken up

blocks.note: a boater is a straw hat
taken as written for mixing

explanation.surface: A rower drifts round a rippling fen as the tide ebbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boater' suggests a person in a boat, but it is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A haaf-net is a fixed bag-net on the Solway, filled with fish as the tide runs out.

clue.text: Crane maybe required to construct Greenwich abode

indicators.note: the letters needed are already present, lying within the following words

blocks.note: spans the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A crane is needed to build a house in Greenwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crane' is not machinery: it is a surname, that of the schoolmaster in Irving's Legend of Sleepy Hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ichabod Crane is the lanky schoolteacher of Washington Irving's tale, so Ichabod is one forename for a Crane.

clue.text: Garrison to house senior service, English

blocks.note: to case is to enclose or house
the Royal Navy is called the Senior Service
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Soldiers stationed to accommodate the navy and the English.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy is Britain's oldest armed service, hence 'senior service'.
explanation.definitionFit: A caserne is a barracks, a building housing a garrison of soldiers in a fortified town.

clue.text: Resinous stuff? Vehicle its association filled with one

indicators.note: something filled with another holds it inside

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
the Automobile Association, the car's own association
un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good un'

explanation.surface: A sticky substance gets on the car, and the motoring body has one to deal with.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation, so it is the car's association.
explanation.definitionFit: Carauna, or caranna, is a soft aromatic resin from South American trees, so a resinous substance.

clue.text: The old king’s mostly laid up in post- prandial periods in Perth

indicators.note: mostly means all but a bit, so the last letter is dropped
in a down entry, lifting up means reading from the bottom

blocks.note: sovran is an archaic form of sovereign

explanation.surface: An old king mostly lies in bed in the afternoons in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: Perth is in Western Australia, so this is Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Arvo is Australian slang for afternoon, the time just after lunch.

clue.text: Topcoat for e.g. legionary, a swell one

blocks.note: taken as written
an old verb meaning to swell into a pod
a means one

explanation.surface: A Roman soldier's coat is described as a fine, swell thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swell' looks like slang for smart but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An abolla was a thick woollen cloak worn in ancient Rome, especially by soldiers.

clue.text: Paul’s correspondents out of gas, found in area round Rome?

indicators.note: out of means lacking, so the stated letters are removed

blocks.note: Paul wrote the Epistle to the Galatians
taken as written, its letters removed one by one

explanation.surface: St Paul's letter-recipients, having run out of gas, end up near Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Latian means of Latium, the ancient region of Italy around Rome.

clue.text: Tidy senior with ragbag put in order

indicators.note: putting something in order arranges it differently, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A neat elderly person sorting out a jumbled bag of odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidy is a container for keeping small items in order, which is what an organiser bag does.

clue.text: One managing bovine stud

blocks.note: first meaning: a manager or employer
second meaning: a dialect word for a cow or calf
third meaning: a raised knob or ornament

explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: 'bovine' too means boss, a dialect name for a cow, so 'bovine stud' is not a breeding bull.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss manages workers, and is also a round protruding knob, the sense matching a decorative stud.

clue.text: Prepare to get hitched? Liz accepting tease

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in

blocks.note: both are short forms of Elizabeth
to rot is to chaff or tease

explanation.surface: Liz is getting ready to marry and puts up with some teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: To betroth is to promise in marriage, the engagement step before the wedding itself.

clue.text: No longer conceal nameless beauty

indicators.note: nameless means without the abbreviation for name, so that letter goes

blocks.note: Helen of Troy, the classic beauty

explanation.surface: A beauty who is no longer hiding, now without a name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No longer' marks the word as obsolete rather than meaning 'stop concealing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hele is an obsolete verb meaning to hide or cover up.

clue.text: Cattle food not applicable for feeding to dog mostly

indicators.note: food fed to an animal goes inside it
mostly means most but not all, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: pooch is slang for a dog
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Animal feed for cattle that should not be given to the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Poonac is coconut oil-cake, the residue after pressing, used in India as fodder for cattle.

clue.text: What dancer may execute, left in a mess

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

blocks.note: pie is printers' type spilt in confusion, a jumble
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A dancer, left in a muddle, tries a move.
explanation.definitionFit: A plié is a ballet movement in which the dancer bends the knees with the back straight.

clue.text: One lives an austere life, being without a modicum of comfort

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed
a modicum is a tiny amount, here just the opening letter

blocks.note: essence is fundamental being
the opening letter of comfort

explanation.surface: An ascetic lives an austere life, existing without even a little comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of the time of Christ, living a strict communal life.

clue.text: Drain installed in urinal (lav)

indicators.note: the letters are lodged within the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of urinal and start of lav

explanation.surface: A drain put in a gents' toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: A lav is British slang for a lavatory, a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A nalla is an Indian word for a ravine or watercourse, hence a drain.

clue.text: Fungus like a sort of lozenge, not red

indicators.note: not means leaving out the stated part

blocks.note: heraldic term: charged with rustres, lozenges pierced with a round hole
taken as written and removed

explanation.surface: A fungus shaped like a lozenge that is not red in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The heraldic term is obscure but in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust is a parasitic fungus causing reddish-brown blotches on plants such as wheat.

clue.text: Old quarter day, day avoided in Lent abed, lazily

indicators.note: something avoided is kept out, so that letter is removed
done lazily, the letters lie about out of order

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spends a holiday lazing in bed during Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: Scottish quarter days are when rents fall due.
explanation.definitionFit: Beltane, 1 May, was an old Scottish quarter day and Celtic festival marked by bonfires.
